newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: BBAG on restructuring drive, merges more brewers.
newsitem.headline: BBAG on restructuring drive, merges more brewers.

text.p: Austrian beverage group BBAG Oesterreichische Brau-Beteiligungs-AG said on Friday it would merge two of its breweries, Steirerbrau and Oesterreichische Brau, in a further restructuring of its brewing operations.
"The goal of the planned integration of Steirerbrau and BrauAG is to attain the level achieved by the best breweries in Europe," BBAG said in a statement.
The two units are 100-percent owned by Brau Union, which in turn is majority-controlled by BBAG.
The new company would have bases in Linz and Graz and would be called Brau Union Oesterreich. Steirerbrau and BrauAG would be equal partners in the new holding.
Since the current brands of the two brewers had a commanding market share and generated good earnings, the new company would continue to sell the original brands.
Preliminary figures for 1996 show that the two brewers together had a 59 percent market share in Austria -- a nation of keen beer drinkers.
The merger would have no impact on any brewing plants -- there were no plans to close any existing breweries, BBAG said.
This latest restructuring comes swift on the heels of BBAG's announcement last month that it would merge its two Hungarian breweries Sopron and Martfu.
The shares of both BBAG and Brau Union were suspended from trading by the Vienna bourse on Friday morning ahead of the announcement.
